reference.title: Hip abduction
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the leg rises, inhale as it lowers.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, 0.5 s hold, 1.7 s down

prescription.progression: Ankle weight, then a band around the knees or ankles

cues.text: Lie on your left side, head on the left arm, hips stacked, legs straight in line with the body.
Breathe out and lift the top leg straight up, toes pointing forward.
Pause at about 35-45 degrees. Leg slightly behind the body line, not in front of it.
Breathe in and lower slowly without resting the leg.
Repeat; then roll over and switch sides.

mistakes.fix: Keep the hips stacked; a hand on the floor in front helps.

mistakes.mistake: Toes turning up to the ceiling
mistakes.fix: Keep the toes forward or slightly down; turning out shifts work to the hip flexors.
Keep the leg in line with the trunk or slightly behind it.
Stop at about 35-45 degrees; higher only hitches the pelvis.

kinematics.norm: Lift to about 35-45 degrees (clinical opinion); side-lying abduction excites the gluteus medius strongly (Distefano 2009; Boren 2011)
Hip neutral to slightly extended, leg in line with the trunk (clinical opinion)
Straight in line, as in the neutral setups compared by Boren 2011 (some protocols bend it for support)
Slow and controlled, slower down than up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: Distefano et al. 2009, gluteal muscle activation during common therapeutic exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 39(7):532-540)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Hip or shoulder pressure on the floor: lie on a mat or bend the bottom knee.
Hard to keep the pelvis stacked: bend the bottom knee and hip for a wider base.

muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Top-leg abductor. Side-lying hip abduction gave the highest gluteus medius activity of the exercises tested by Distefano 2009 (about 81% MVIC); Boren 2011 measured about 63% MVIC.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Upper fibres assist abduction with the hip neutral; Boren 2011 measured about 51% MVIC in side-lying abduction.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Keep the pelvis stacked so it does not roll back as the leg rises (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Keep the pelvis stacked so it does not roll back as the leg rises (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Holds the trunk still on the mat (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Top leg lifts in line with the body
